description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and IKE—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy in percentage from 60% to 80%. The Base method, represented by black circles connected by a solid line, shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 64% at a co-occurrence number of 1 to about 70% at 1000. The MEND method, shown with brown diamonds and a solid line, starts at around 69% and rises to approximately 77% at 1000. The FT method, indicated by blue triangles and a solid line, begins at roughly 65% and increases to about 72% at 1000. The MEMIT method, depicted with purple squares and a solid line, starts at approximately 68% and climbs to around 76% at 1000. The IKE method, represented by red triangles and a solid line, begins at about 66% and increases to approximately 73% at 1000. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with the IKE method consistently achieving the highest accuracy across the range of co-occurrence numbers.
